original_question: Does the marked length spectrum determine such a metric (in the class of all locally CAT (−1) metrics on this space, or in the class of all 2-dimensional (metrical) simplicial complexes with the above properties homeomorphic to the given complex)?
target_in_paper: Question 5.1.2 (Benjamin Schmidt) in §5.1: the marked-length-spectrum rigidity question for a 2-dimensional metrical simplicial complex whose simplices are hyperbolic with geodesic edges, with the CAT(-1) condition at every vertex, and with every edge contained in at least two simplices. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s exact target and preserves the two comparison classes almost verbatim: rigidity among all locally CAT(-1) metrics on the fixed space, and rigidity among all 2-dimensional metrical simplicial complexes with the same local properties that are homeomorphic to the original complex. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
missing_details: It omits the antecedent of "such a metric": the object under discussion is a 2-dimensional metrical simplicial complex. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
It omits the simplex-level hypothesis that every simplex is hyperbolic and has geodesic edges. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
It omits the curvature hypothesis in the setup: the CAT(-1) condition must hold at every vertex. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
It omits the combinatorial hypothesis that every edge is contained in at least two simplices. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

It does not define the marked length spectrum, which in the immediately preceding paragraph is the function sending each free homotopy class of loops to the infimum of the lengths of loops in that class. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

To make the question fully stand-alone, it helps to state explicitly that "determine" is meant in the rigidity sense suggested by the immediately preceding Conjecture 5.1.1: uniqueness up to isometry for metrics with the same marked length spectrum. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

It does not mention nearby scope information from the paper: the topological-manifold case is already known to have a positive answer, and the paper separately notes an easier variant where every edge lies in at least three simplices. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
refined_question: Let X be a 2-dimensional metrical simplicial complex such that every simplex of X is hyperbolic with geodesic edges, the CAT(-1) condition holds at every vertex, and every edge is contained in at least two simplices. If the marked length spectrum of X is the function assigning to each free homotopy class of loops in X the infimum of the lengths of loops in that class, does this marked length spectrum determine the metric uniquely up to isometry, either among all locally CAT(-1) metrics on the fixed space X, or among all 2-dimensional metrical simplicial complexes with the same three properties that are homeomorphic to X? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
justification: The draft is essentially the official Question 5.1.2, but it is not stand-alone because it drops the setup sentence that specifies the class of simplicial complexes and it also omits the preceding definition of marked length spectrum. I made the implicit rigidity meaning of "determine" explicit as uniqueness up to isometry because §5.1 introduces the analogous manifold statement in Conjecture 5.1.1 in exactly that form. I did not fold in the known manifold case or the "at least three simplices per edge" variant, because the paper presents those only as surrounding remarks, not as the main question itself. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
